title: Make a waffle in a rotating waffle maker: pour the batter, latch the lid, turn it over, turn it back and open it
instruction: Make a waffle: pour the cup of batter onto the waffle grid, close and latch the lid, turn the waffle maker over and leave it to bake, then turn it back and open the lid.
context: Rotating Belgian waffle makers stand on hotel breakfast buffets, where guests make their own waffles. Waring WW180 manual: "Fill measuring scoop with batter to fill line. Pour batter evenly into the center of the waffle grid ... Close the lid and rotate the unit 180 degrees"; when it beeps, "rotate the waffle maker 180 degrees, open the lid and remove waffle". On models with a lid latch: "Make sure your lid has latched into place ... Turn the handle so that the waffle plates flip 180 degrees." The hand skill: a cup of batter poured over its lip onto an 18 cm grid; the open lid tipped over so it falls shut and pressed at its handle until the latch clicks (10 N); the handle pinched and turned 180 deg about its own axis, a full wrist roll; let go while it bakes; turned back; the handle pulled up against the latch (17 N) to lift the lid. Turned over unlatched, the lid swings open underneath and the batter falls out. One arm does most of it; the other tips the lid shut.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Rotating Belgian waffle maker (like the Waring WW180), fixed (about 6 kg on rubber feet), unplugged and cold: base plate 26 x 30 x 2 cm centred at x 25, y 12; the housing turns on a shaft along y at x 25, 14.5 cm up, carried by a post at the rear (y 24.5). Housing 23 cm across, centred at y 9.5, two halves 4.5 cm thick meeting at 14.5 cm, each with an 18 cm (7-inch) Belgian grid 1.2 cm deep; bottom half 2.4 kg, lid 1.2 kg, hinged along x at y 21, 14.5 cm up. The lid's handle, 11 cm long, 3 cm wide, 2.6 cm deep, runs out along the shaft's axis to y -12.5. The housing rests on stops at 0 and 180 deg. The lid starts standing open, just past its balance point. A spring catch latches the lid (below). (2) Batter cup: stainless, no handle, 7.6 cm across the top, 6.0 cm at the base, 7.5 cm tall, 0.12 kg, at x 21, y -18, holding 30 batter beads 10 mm across, 8 g each (240 g). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: "In" = 27 or more of the 30 beads on the grid (over the 18 cm grid, between the two grids). 0.25 the lid closed (within 2 deg) with the batter in; 0.5 latched (the closed lid pressed down with 10 N, housing upright) with the batter in; 0.75 turned over (175 deg or more), latched, batter in, and left 3 s with every finger 3 cm or more from the waffle maker (the bake, shortened); 1.0 (success, held 1 s) after that, turned back within 5 deg of upright, the lid unlatched and open 30 deg or more, batter in. 0 for the whole run once the lid opens 20 deg or more while the housing is turned more than 60 deg. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the video, and the batter on the grid at the end.
reset_notes: Open the lid back onto its stop with the housing upright, wipe the grids and the table, put the cup back at its mark and refill it with the 30 beads (real trial with batter: 240 g of pancake-mix batter, about 1 cup, mixed fresh; wipe the grids clean between trials). Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The unit is cold: no heating, the bake is 3 s hands-off. Batter is 30 rigid 10 mm beads. The latch is a rule: it clicks when the closed lid is pressed down with 10 N (PhysX contact force), then holds the lid (300 N m/rad) until it is pulled open 0.5 deg, about 17 N at the handle; these forces are estimates, measure them on the real unit. The lid is opened 30 deg, not fully: past about 45 deg its handle is out of the arms' reach.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the waffle maker instead of the batter cup, knocking the open lid shut on the empty grid and pushing at the housing; it never picked up the cup, so no batter reached the grid); demo: 1.0
